chapter: Playing in New Orleans and influences
title: Jobs with Kid Thomas and Lutcher's, and Belfast and Cambridge bands
summary: He played at Luthjen's, with Kid Thomas, and recalls Bill McCleche and his own Cambridge band.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: have you uh played any jobs or just sat in uh with uh many of the the old timers and in the dance halls just sessions or dance yeah i played at lutchins and with kid thomas he was on and off

uh played at lutchins with uh diddy and uh billy piers you know those two yeah and then talker took over i played with talker for a little bit and then he left and they got a band it wasn't really they i don't know what they've got up there now they didn't sound like jazz and i played with kid thomas at the moulin rouge and at the tip top and then i went to play at uh play with them at the uh fireman's hall the west wiga fireman's hall but the banter at the fireman's hall is the jefferson parish jailer yeah he wouldn't let me play so that was too bad yeah another irish fellow was over here bill mccleche played the bass i used to play with him in belfast on vacations from cambridge and uh he played bass with kid thomas they really loved him he played hard when was he here oh last winter the winter before last he went off to new zealand he emigrated to new zealand via new orleans i had a band see when i was in college in the university at cambridge i played in my first year there i played with the university jazz band then i started my own band up um and in the vacations i would go back to belfast and play with this little band that this fellow mccleche had started up they were straight in the uh bunk johnson uh tradition and he was the first guy ever played me an american music record he played me the wooden joe record they'd been smuggled into the country by a man called solly lipsitz and have since been confiscated by the british uh customs and excise for not yeah it was confiscated off him that's terrible oh i had a band at cambridge used to run dances of my own in the masonic hall cambridge masonic hall in the summer vacation when there were only one or two people and a lot of foreigners there did pretty well had a dixieland band of trombone a fellow that tried to imitate dodds on clarinet and took murphy imitator on trombone you know that kind of thing very fat fellow with 21 stones 21 multiplied by 14 to gain pounds over 300
